answer: Verifiable Effort Ledger. Each identity must forge a unique history of solved micro-tasks whose answers depend on a slow external clock, so histories cannot be purchased or mass-produced in parallel. A raven token is issued only when a verifier replays that history and finds the timing gaps consistent with real sequential work. Any clone must pay the full wall-clock cost again, and a reused relic from an old ledger is rejected at replay, so scaling identities costs linear human-attention hours rather than money.
